acceptance_criteria.criterion: `registerWorkspaceRoutes()` accepts an `ErrorLogManager` parameter (6th argument), and `index.ts` passes it.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` returns 404 when the workspace does not exist.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` returns 400 with `"Workspace file does not exist. Run setup first."` when the `.code-workspace` file is missing from disk.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` returns `200 { success: true }` when the file exists and the launch succeeds.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` returns 404 when the workspace or project/repository is not found.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` returns 400 with `"Repository directory does not exist. Run setup first."` when the repo directory is missing.
`POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` returns `200 { success: true }` when the directory exists and the launch succeeds.

On launch failure, both endpoints return 500 with a descriptive error message and log an entry to the error log with `Source: 'app-launcher'` and appropriate `Operation`, `Severity: 'error'`, `Context`, and `Message` fields.

summary: Reviewed 5 files (workspaces.ts, index.ts, app-launcher.ts, error-log.manager.ts, router.ts). All OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 2 Medium observations recorded (path traversal defence could be hardened with explicit normalisation; error message disclosure in 500 paths). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03/A01 — Path Traversal (defence-in-depth gap): workspaces.ts lines 403 and 462. Both new handlers construct filesystem paths by joining `appConfig.projectsFolder`, `projectId`, `workspaceId`, and (for github-desktop) `repoId` via `path.join()`. These values originate from URL parameters extracted by the router. The router's `extractParams()` captures raw URL path segments without percent-decoding or normalisation — a segment value of `..` would survive extraction. For the github-desktop handler, `project.Repositories.includes(repoId)` provides the primary guard (the repository must be in the project's allow-list), so traversal via `repoId` is effectively blocked as long as ID values are validated at creation time (confirmed by QA). For `projectId` and `workspaceId`, there is no explicit traversal check in these two new handlers; traversal is only blocked indirectly by `workspaceManager.getById()` / `projectManager.getById()` lookup failures — callers can only reach a path if the manager returns a valid record for those IDs. This layered defence is adequate for the current localhost-only threat model, but adding explicit `path.resolve()` + `startsWith(appConfig.projectsFolder)` assertions would remove all doubt and future-proof the code if the server ever moves to a networked deployment. Remediation: add a guard such as `if (!resolvedPath.startsWith(path.resolve(appConfig.projectsFolder))) { sendError(res, 400, 'Invalid path.'); return; }` after constructing `wsFilePath` (line 403) and `repoDir` (line 462).

A05 — Error Message Information Disclosure: workspaces.ts lines 413 and 472. On launch failure, the raw `err.message` from `launchApplication` is forwarded directly to the HTTP response body (500) AND to the error log. The launcher error messages include the executable name (e.g. `Failed to launch application "code": spawn code ENOENT`). In a multi-user or network-accessible environment this would disclose internal path structure. In the current threat model (localhost single-user CLI tool, server binds to 127.0.0.1 per index.ts:176) this is low practical risk, but is worth noting. Remediation: consider mapping internal error messages to a generic user-facing message (e.g. `'Failed to launch VS Code. Ensure VS Code is installed and available on PATH.'`) while preserving the full message only in the error log entry.

A09 — Security Logging Coverage: Both new handlers log errors to ErrorLogManager on 500, with well-structured fields (Source, Operation, Severity, Context including ProjectId/WorkspaceId/RepositoryId). No gaps identified. Logging is absent for 400/404 responses, consistent with the existing codebase pattern — these are client errors and do not represent security events in this context.

A07 — Authentication/Authorization: These endpoints perform no authentication or session checks — consistent with the rest of the codebase. The server binds exclusively to 127.0.0.1 (index.ts line 176), restricting access to the local machine. No auth gap introduced by the new endpoints.

A06 — Dependencies: No new third-party dependencies were introduced. The implementation uses only Node.js built-ins (`node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`) and existing internal modules. No CVE exposure added.

A08 — Software & Data Integrity / Command Injection: app-launcher.ts uses `spawn()` with `shell: false` on non-Windows platforms, which prevents shell injection via the args array. On Windows, `shell: true` is used for `.cmd` launcher compatibility — the `command` argument is a hardcoded string literal ('code' or 'github') supplied by the route handler, not user-controlled input, so shell injection is not a risk in practice.

Full OWASP Top 10 review summary: A01 (Access Control) — workspace/project membership validated before filesystem access; A02 (Crypto) — no cryptographic operations introduced; A03 (Injection) — spawn args are derived from validated IDs + config paths, not raw user input; A04 (Insecure Design) — guard ordering is correct (entity existence before disk check before launch); A05 (Misconfiguration) — stack traces not leaked, generic 500 messages used except for launcher errors (noted above); A06 (Components) — no new deps; A07 (Auth) — localhost-only server, no regression; A08 (Integrity) — no unsafe deserialization or unsigned updates; A09 (Logging) — error log entries correctly structured; A10 (SSRF) — no outbound HTTP requests; no server-side URL fetching introduced.
